eo-14028.summary: The root of most current federal cyber operations requirements: zero trust architecture, endpoint detection and response (EDR), event logging, secure software development, a standard incident-response playbook, and the Cyber Safety Review Board. The order sets direction; OMB and CISA issue the actual requirements.
eo-14028.forYou: Nothing new is owed under the order itself — the work lives in its children. Zero trust (M-22-09), EDR (M-22-01) and logging (now M-26-14, which replaced M-21-31) all trace back here. When someone asks 'what authority?', this is usually the answer.
eo-14028.statusNote: Amended by EO 14144 (Jan 16, 2025), which was itself substantially cut back by EO 14306 (June 6, 2025).

actions.text: Track the child memos for live deadlines: M-26-14 (logging), M-22-09 (zero trust), M-22-01 (EDR), M-26-05 (software security, which rescinded the attestation form).

eo-14028.author: claude-draft

eo-14144.summary: Late-term Biden order adding software-attestation enforcement, digital identity, PQC planning, and other cyber requirements. EO 14306 struck a large share of it five months later; what survives is mostly the PQC/TLS and AI-vulnerability provisions as rewritten by EO 14306.
eo-14144.forYou: Read it only through EO 14306. If a vendor or an older internal plan cites EO 14144 for a requirement, check that the section survived the June 2025 amendments before you spend money on it.

actions.text: Before acting on any EO 14144 citation, confirm the section still exists after EO 14306.

eo-14144.author: claude-draft

eo-14306.summary: Trims EO 14144 and keeps a short list of requirements: TLS 1.3 support by January 2, 2030; a CISA list of product categories that support post-quantum cryptography (due December 1, 2025); a NIST update to the Secure Software Development Framework (preliminary by December 1, 2025); and AI-vulnerability handling. It also narrows the cyber sanctions order (EO 13694) to foreign persons.
eo-14306.forYou: The TLS 1.3 date is yours. Every load balancer, reverse proxy, VPN concentrator, web server and API gateway OIT runs has to support TLS 1.3 (or a successor) by January 2, 2030. That's a refresh-cycle problem, not a configuration problem, for anything that can't be upgraded.

actions.text: Support TLS 1.3 (or a successor) on agency systems as soon as practicable and no later than January 2, 2030. Start with an inventory of TLS termination points (F5/ADC, proxies, VPN, web/API front ends) and flag any that can't do 1.3.
Use CISA's list of product categories that support post-quantum cryptography when you specify new hardware or software in those categories.
Expect NIST's updated SSDF (SP 800-218) to flow into software acquisition language — paired with M-26-05's risk-based approach rather than a mandatory form.
actions.dueNote: Preliminary update due Dec 1, 2025; final 120 days later

eo-14306.author: claude-draft

eo-14412.summary: Sets the first hard federal post-quantum cryptography (PQC) deadlines. Agencies name a PQC Migration Lead within 30 days. High-value assets and high-impact systems move key establishment to PQC by December 31, 2030 and digital signatures by December 31, 2031. NIST and CISA define minimum elements of a Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM), and the FAR Council proposes a rule requiring covered contractors to use FIPS-validated PQC by 2030. OMB M-26-15 turns this into a five-phase plan.
eo-14412.forYou: IT Ops owns where the cryptography actually lives: TLS termination, VPN, SSH, PKI, HSMs, code signing, and every appliance with a baked-in crypto library. The inventory is the long pole, and M-26-15's migration plan depended on it.

actions.text: Confirm who DFC named as PQC Migration Lead (due within 30 days of signing) and how OIT feeds them.
Build and maintain a cryptographic inventory for HVAs and high-impact systems: protocols, algorithms, key sizes, libraries and the device or service that terminates each.
Move key establishment on HVAs and high-impact systems to PQC by December 31, 2030.
Move digital signatures on HVAs and high-impact systems to PQC by December 31, 2031.
Watch for the FAR proposed rule requiring covered contractors to comply with FIPS PQC by December 31, 2030. It will reach your vendors' hosted services and your contractor-operated systems.

eo-14412.author: claude-draft

eo-14409.summary: An AI-and-security order with 30- and 60-day taskings. Treasury, NSA and CISA set up an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse. OPM expands 'Tech Force' cybersecurity hiring pathways within 60 days. Agencies are told to expedite and prioritize cyber defense of civilian federal systems. Frontier-model reviews are voluntary; the order says it creates no pre-clearance requirement.
eo-14409.forYou: Two practical angles. As a manager, the expanded cyber hiring pathways may be your fastest legal route to backfill a cyber or IT position, if the Strategic Hiring Committee approves it. As IT Ops, expect data calls on cyber posture under the 'expedite and prioritize' language.

actions.text: Ask HR whether OPM's expanded Tech Force cybersecurity pathways are live, before you write your next justification for the Strategic Hiring Committee.
actions.dueNote: 60 days after signing (OPM's deadline, not yours)

actions.text: Expect CISA and OMB data calls on civilian-system defenses. Keep EDR coverage, logging status and KEV remediation metrics current.

eo-14158.summary: Renames USDS as the U.S. DOGE Service, creates a temporary organization inside it (which ended July 4, 2026), requires each agency to stand up a DOGE Team of at least four people, and launches a Software Modernization Initiative. Agency heads must give USDS full and prompt access to all unclassified agency records, software systems and IT systems, to the extent the law allows.
eo-14158.forYou: When access requests come from the DOGE Team, OIT executes them. Handle them like any privileged access: written approval from the agency head or CIO designee, least privilege, named accounts, logging, and an ISA or Privacy Act review where the system needs one. Keep a record. If anyone later asks who had access to what, the answer comes out of your account logs.
eo-14158.statusNote: USDS (the U.S. DOGE Service) continues. The temporary organization terminated July 4, 2026 under §3(b).

actions.text: Provision USDS/DOGE Team access to unclassified records, software and IT systems when the agency head directs it. Use documented approvals, least privilege, logging and periodic review.
Support the Software Modernization Initiative (interoperability, data integrity, data synchronization) when the DOGE Team or USDS asks.
Know who is on DFC's DOGE Team (at least four employees) and who in leadership approves their requests.

eo-14158.author: claude-draft

eo-14243.summary: Directs agency heads to ensure that designated federal officials have full and prompt access to unclassified agency records, data, software systems and IT systems for detecting waste, fraud and abuse, and to rescind or modify guidance that blocks intra- and inter-agency data sharing, to the extent the law allows.
eo-14243.forYou: Same playbook as EO 14158, but the requests may come from officials outside the DOGE Team and may involve bulk data movement. Insist on written designation, a documented legal basis (Privacy Act/SORN, ISA), and logging. That protects you as much as the data.

actions.text: Fulfil designated officials' access and data-sharing requests with written authorization, a documented legal basis and logging.
Flag OIT-owned policies or ISAs that restrict internal data sharing, if leadership runs a review under this order.

Expect every invoice to need a short written justification in the agency's payment-justification system, and every option or recompete to face termination-or-justify scrutiny. Keep a one-paragraph mission justification on hand for each contract and labor category.

Keep a current justification for each OIT contract: mission need, labor categories, cost and what breaks if it is cut. You will be asked again.
actions.dueNote: Initial review was due within 30 days (Mar 28, 2025)

eo-14240.author: claude-draft

actions.text: List every OIT contract that delivers LLM capability. Confirm with the CO that M-26-04 terms are in place before the next option.

eo-14210.summary: Orders agencies to prepare large-scale reductions in force (RIFs) and reorganizations (Agency RIF and Reorganization Plans, ARRPs), limits hiring to roughly one hire per four departures, and gives the DOGE Team a role in hiring decisions.
eo-14210.forYou: Two hats. As a manager, the ARRP data calls asked about your positions and functions, and hiring now runs through EO 14356's committee. As an employee, RIF authority is live: the Supreme Court stayed the injunction against ARRP-based RIFs in July 2025.

litigation.status: Injunction stayed July 8, 2025. RIFs may proceed.

Earlier freeze exemptions stay in place unless OPM withdraws them.
eo-14356.forYou: Every federal backfill or new position in OIT now needs committee approval tied to mission and administration priorities. With three direct reports and two second-line, a single departure is a big share of your team. Have the justification written before you need it.

actions.text: Submit a Strategic Hiring Committee request (mission need, priority alignment, cost) for any OIT federal vacancy you want to create or fill.
Supply OIT's input to the annual staffing plan and quarterly updates (positions, projected departures, critical skills).
Pre-write justifications for your three direct-report positions now, so a departure doesn't start from zero.

eo-14356.author: claude-draft

Your 29 contractor staff are not covered; their place of performance comes from their contracts, so any change goes through the CO, not this memo. With a bargaining unit, check whether DFC's CBA telework terms still apply. That depends on EO 14251 (see that entry).
